newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU inflation at record low 2.2 percent in November.
newsitem.headline: EU inflation at record low 2.2 percent in November.

text.p: Inflation in the European Union stood at a meagre 2.2 percent in November, the lowest level on record since 1983, the EU's statistical office Eurostat said Monday.
The latest result compared with a 2.4 percent advance in prices in the 15-nation bloc during October and a 2.3 percent rise in September.
In Sweden, prices actually fell by 0.3 percent in November, while Greece showed the strongest rise in inflation at 7.7 percent.

Separately, Eurostat also published interim indices of consumer prices which seek to give a glimpse of the progress countries are making toward meeting the inflation criterion for economic and monetary union. The indices are intended to provide a better basis for comparison than the national inflation figures, as certain categories of expenditure have been excluded while others have been added.

According to the latest survey, EU inflation stood at 2.3 percent in November, with Sweden showing a slight 0.2 percent rise in prices. Greece, meanwhile, put in a somewhat better performance with inflation advancing at 7.3 percent.
The EU is still working toward a fully harmonised index that will be used in determining which countries qualify for EMU.
